reconstructed_captions.34: A hand uses a wooden slicker to burnish the sealed edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.35: A multi-pronged pricking iron is aligned on the leather to mark stitching holes.
reconstructed_captions.36: A mallet strikes the pricking iron, punching a row of stitching holes through the leather.
reconstructed_captions.37: A close-up shows the evenly spaced, angled stitching holes created by the tool.
reconstructed_captions.38: The black leather piece is clamped firmly into a wooden stitching pony.
reconstructed_captions.39: A hand begins to saddle stitch the leather pieces together using two needles.
reconstructed_captions.40: A close-up shows a needle with waxed thread passing through a pre-punched hole.
reconstructed_captions.41: The second needle is passed through the same hole from the opposite side.
reconstructed_captions.42: The threads are pulled tight, creating a strong and durable lock stitch.
reconstructed_captions.43: The hand-stitching continues methodically along the seam of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.44: The final stitches are backstitched to secure the end of the seam.
reconstructed_captions.45: A sharp knife is used to carefully trim the excess thread flush with the leather.
reconstructed_captions.46: The stitched leather edge is sanded with a sanding block to make it smooth and even.
reconstructed_captions.47: A close-up shows the fine dust being created as the leather edge is sanded.
reconstructed_captions.48: The leather dust is wiped off the edge with a cloth, preparing it for finishing.
reconstructed_captions.49: A hand applies another layer of sealing liquid to the smooth, sanded edge.
reconstructed_captions.50: A hand uses an edge beveling tool to round off the sharp corners of the leather edge.
reconstructed_captions.51: The edge beveler shaves off a thin strip of leather, creating a clean, rounded profile.
